questions.q: A red blood cell is placed in distilled water. Distilled water contains no dissolved solutes. What happens to the red blood cell, and why?
options: It shrinks because water leaves the cell by osmosis.
It stays the same because the cell wall prevents it from bursting.
It bursts because glucose is actively transported into the cell.
It swells and bursts because water enters the cell by osmosis.
questions.explanation: Distilled water has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm, so water enters the red blood cell by osmosis. Red blood cells have no cell wall, so the cell swells and bursts rather than staying the same.

questions.q: A muscle cell and a skin cell from the same person have the same genes. Which statement best explains why they have different shapes and carry out different functions?
options: Each cell contains a different set of genes suited to its function.
Different genes are switched on in each cell, so different proteins are made.
Skin cells have lost all their genetic material as they mature.
Only muscle cells contain mitochondria for respiration.
questions.explanation: All body cells from the same person contain the same genes, but different genes are switched on in different cell types. This selective gene expression produces different proteins, giving muscle and skin cells their different structures and functions.

questions.q: Which component of blood is mainly responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to respiring tissues?
options: Red blood cells containing haemoglobin
White blood cells that engulf pathogens
Platelets that help blood to clot
Plasma that transports carbon dioxide to the lungs
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it in respiring tissues. White blood cells defend against pathogens, platelets clot blood, and plasma transports many dissolved substances but is not the main oxygen carrier.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the action of bile in the digestive system?
options: It absorbs water from the large intestine into the blood.
It digests fats into glycerol and fatty acids by hydrolysis.
It breaks down starch into sugars in the small intestine.
It emulsifies fats into smaller droplets and neutralises acidic food from the stomach.
questions.explanation: Bile emulsifies fats into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase, and it neutralises acidic food entering the small intestine from the stomach. It does not contain digestive enzymes, so it does not itself hydrolyse fats or starch.

questions.q: Which balanced symbol equation represents aerobic respiration?
options: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6CO₂ → 6O₂ + 6H₂O
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration uses glucose and oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water. The equation C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O correctly balances these substances.

questions.q: What is the main function of chlorophyll in a leaf cell?
options: It absorbs water from the soil for the plant.
It joins carbon dioxide to oxygen to make glucose.
It reflects all visible light so that the leaf appears green.
It absorbs light energy for use in photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy, mainly red and blue light, which is used to drive photosynthesis in chloroplasts. It mostly reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.

questions.q: A healthy plant has plenty of carbon dioxide and bright light, but it is kept at 5 °C. Its rate of photosynthesis is much lower than at 25 °C. Which explanation is most likely?
options: The low temperature slows the enzymes that control photosynthesis.
The bright light causes the stomata to close completely.
The plant cannot absorb any carbon dioxide at low temperatures.
Chlorophyll is permanently destroyed by cool conditions.
questions.explanation: At 5 °C, the kinetic energy of molecules is lower and the enzymes controlling photosynthesis work more slowly, so the rate is lower. The plant still has light and carbon dioxide, so low temperature is the limiting factor here.

questions.q: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, the grass contains 80,000 kJ of energy. If 10% of the energy is transferred to the rabbit, and 10% of the rabbit's energy is transferred to the fox, how much energy is transferred to the fox?
options: 800 kJ
80 kJ
questions.explanation: The rabbit receives 10% of 80,000 kJ, which is 80,000 × 0.10 = 8,000 kJ. The fox then receives 10% of that energy, 8,000 × 0.10 = 800 kJ. Most energy is lost between trophic levels through respiration, movement and heat.

questions.q: Lichen species are sensitive to sulfur dioxide in the air. A survey finds that the number of lichen species in an area has fallen over 20 years. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Air pollution, especially sulfur dioxide, has increased.
More sulfur dioxide has been removed by rainwater, making the habitat less suitable.
Oxygen levels have fallen, so lichens cannot carry out respiration.
Less sulfur dioxide is present, so lichens cannot photosynthesise.
questions.explanation: Lichens are indicator species for air pollution; many species cannot tolerate high concentrations of sulfur dioxide. A fall in lichen species therefore most likely indicates that sulfur dioxide pollution has increased.

questions.q: Which adaptation most directly reduces water loss from the leaves of a plant living in a hot, dry desert?
options: A very large leaf surface area to absorb more sunlight
A thick waxy cuticle on the leaf surface
Brightly coloured flowers to attract many insects
Many stomata on the upper surface of large, flat leaves
questions.explanation: A thick waxy cuticle is waterproof and reduces evaporation from the leaf surface, helping to conserve water in a hot, dry habitat. Large flat leaves, many upper-surface stomata and showy flowers do not directly reduce water loss from leaves.

questions.q: Why does a vaccination usually protect a person from a disease without causing the illness?
options: It contains memory cells taken from another person, which immediately destroy the pathogen.
It exposes the immune system to antigens from a dead, inactive or harmless pathogen, so white blood cells make antibodies and memory cells without causing disease.
It contains antibiotics that remain in the blood and kill the pathogen before symptoms appear.
It makes the skin waterproof so pathogens cannot enter the body.
questions.explanation: The vaccine acts as a safe stimulus for the immune system. White blood cells produce specific antibodies and memory cells, so a later infection is fought quickly. Antibiotics do not create immunity, and memory cells are made by the person’s immune system rather than supplied ready-made in the vaccine.

questions.q: In pea plants, the allele for tall stems (T) is dominant to the allele for short stems (t). A heterozygous tall plant is crossed with a short plant. What percentage of the offspring are expected to be short?
questions.explanation: The tall parent can pass on either T or t, while the short parent can pass on only t. The possible offspring are Tt and tt in equal numbers, so half are tt and show the short stem. A 25% result would come from crossing two heterozygous tall plants, not a tall plant with a short plant.

questions.q: On an island, a population of birds becomes separated from the mainland population for many generations. Over time, the island birds can no longer interbreed with the mainland birds. Which process best explains how this could happen?
options: Natural selection acting in different environments changes allele frequencies until the two populations become reproductively isolated.
The island birds deliberately change their genes so that they can survive better.
The mainland birds stop producing gametes, so no interbreeding is possible.
A single bird grows a new beak shape and all its offspring inherit it during its lifetime.
questions.explanation: Different environmental conditions can select different inherited variations, so allele frequencies in each population change over time. Eventually, the populations may become so different that they cannot interbreed to produce fertile offspring, which is speciation. Deliberate change or changes acquired during life are not inherited as genetic adaptations.

questions.q: A farmer wants to produce a herd of cows that give more milk over many generations. Which method is selective breeding rather than genetic engineering?
options: Insert a milk-producing gene from another species into cow embryos.
Choose cows that give the most milk and breed them with bulls from high-milk-producing parents, repeating the process over generations.
Clone one high-milk cow so that all the offspring are genetically identical.
Expose cows to radiation so that new milk-yield mutations appear randomly.
questions.explanation: Selective breeding relies on choosing parents with desirable inherited characteristics and allowing them to reproduce, so useful alleles become more common in later generations. Genetic engineering would involve transferring a gene directly between organisms, while cloning produces genetically identical offspring without changing allele frequencies by selection. Radiation induces random mutations rather than selecting existing high-yield cows.

questions.q: Pancreatic cells secrete digestive enzymes. Which cell structure is most directly responsible for making these protein molecules?
options: Cell membrane
Ribosomes
Large permanent vacuole
Mitochondria
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, and proteins are assembled on ribosomes using amino acids. Mitochondria release energy for the process but do not synthesise the protein molecules. The large permanent vacuole is a plant cell structure, and the cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.

questions.q: Which statement distinguishes a prokaryotic cell from a eukaryotic cell?
options: A prokaryotic cell is always larger and contains many mitochondria.
A prokaryotic cell has a cellulose cell wall, while a eukaryotic cell never has a cell wall.
A prokaryotic cell has no membrane-bound nucleus, while a eukaryotic cell has a nucleus containing DNA.
A prokaryotic cell reproduces only by mitosis, while a eukaryotic cell reproduces only by meiosis.
questions.explanation: The key difference is that prokaryotic cells do not have a membrane-bound nucleus, so their genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm, often as circular DNA. Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. Mitochondria are not found in prokaryotes, and many eukaryotic cells can divide by mitosis as well as meiosis.

questions.q: A student examines a thin section of a leaf. One tissue is found near the upper surface and contains many chloroplasts in closely packed cells. What is the main function of this tissue?
options: Absorbing light energy for photosynthesis
Storing starch in dead, lignified cells
Allowing carbon dioxide to diffuse into the leaf through stomata
Transporting water and mineral ions to the leaf
questions.explanation: The tissue described is palisade mesophyll. Its closely packed cells contain many chloroplasts, which absorb light energy for photosynthesis. Xylem transports water and mineral ions, while gas exchange occurs mainly through stomata and air spaces in the spongy mesophyll.

questions.q: In the digestive system, which enzyme breaks down proteins into amino acids?
options: Protease
Lipase
Catalase
Amylase
questions.explanation: Proteases break down proteins into amino acids, which can then be absorbed. Amylase digests starch to sugars, lipase digests fats to fatty acids and glycerol, and catalase breaks down hydrogen peroxide.

questions.q: A healthy plant is kept in bright light. A student claims that the plant only respires at night. Which statement best explains why this claim is incorrect?
options: Respiration happens all the time; in bright light photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide faster than respiration produces it.
Plants release oxygen only in darkness because respiration stops.
Respiration happens only when the plant has no chlorophyll.
Photosynthesis replaces respiration completely during daylight.
questions.explanation: Respiration is continuous in living plant cells and does not stop in the light. In bright light, photosynthesis usually uses carbon dioxide faster than respiration releases it, so the plant has a net uptake of carbon dioxide and releases oxygen.

questions.q: A sealed tube contains germinating seeds and a carbon dioxide indicator. It is kept in the dark, with plenty of oxygen present. After 30 minutes, the indicator shows carbon dioxide is being released. Which process is mainly responsible?
options: Anaerobic respiration in the seeds
Transpiration from the seeds
Photosynthesis in the seeds
Aerobic respiration in the seeds
questions.explanation: Germinating seeds respire aerobically when oxygen is present, using oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide. The tube is in the dark, so photosynthesis cannot occur, and anaerobic respiration is not the main process while plenty of oxygen remains.

questions.q: A student records that a muscle releases 72 kJ of energy from aerobic respiration and 18 kJ from anaerobic respiration during exercise. What percentage of the total energy released is from anaerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: The total energy released is 72 kJ + 18 kJ = 90 kJ. The anaerobic fraction is (18 kJ ÷ 90 kJ) × 100 = 20%.

questions.q: In a food chain, only a small fraction of the energy in one trophic level is transferred to the next. Which statement best explains why food chains rarely have more than five trophic levels?
options: About 90% of the energy is transferred to the next trophic level, so food chains can only last five levels.
Energy is lost at each level, mainly as heat during respiration and in uneaten or excreted material, so too little remains at higher levels.
Higher-level consumers use no energy for respiration, so they cannot support another trophic level.
Energy is recycled by decomposers back to the first trophic level, so top predators receive very little energy.
questions.explanation: At each trophic level, a large proportion of energy is lost as heat during respiration and in uneaten or excreted material, and only about 10% is transferred to the next level. After several transfers, too little energy remains to support another population, so food chains are usually short.

questions.q: A thick tree canopy blocks sunlight above small green plants on a woodland floor. Which abiotic factor is most directly reduced for these plants by the canopy?
options: Oxygen concentration in the air
Light intensity
Soil water content
Soil mineral ion concentration
questions.explanation: The canopy intercepts sunlight, so the light intensity reaching plants on the woodland floor is greatly reduced. Light is needed for photosynthesis, so it is the factor most directly limited by the canopy.

questions.q: In a vaccine trial, 500 vaccinated people and 500 unvaccinated people are observed for six months. During this time, 20 vaccinated people and 100 unvaccinated people catch the disease. For every vaccinated person who caught the disease, how many unvaccinated people caught it?
options: 100 unvaccinated people
20 unvaccinated people
4 unvaccinated people
5 unvaccinated people
questions.explanation: Both groups contain 500 people, so the numbers of cases can be compared directly: 100 ÷ 20 = 5. Equivalently, 20% of the unvaccinated group caught the disease compared with 4% of the vaccinated group, a ratio of 5:1.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the function of ribosomes in a cell?
options: They are the site of protein synthesis.
They contain the genetic material and control the cell's activities.
They release energy from glucose during aerobic respiration.
They control which substances enter and leave the cell.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes assemble amino acids into proteins. Mitochondria release energy from glucose, the cell membrane controls movement of substances, and the nucleus contains the genetic material.

questions.q: During the cell cycle, when is the DNA in a body cell replicated?
options: During cytokinesis, as the cytoplasm divides.
During prophase, while the chromosomes become visible.
During interphase, before mitosis begins.
After mitosis, when each daughter cell has separated.
questions.explanation: DNA is replicated during interphase so that each daughter cell receives an identical copy of the genetic material. In prophase the chromosomes condense and become visible, while cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm.

questions.q: A plant cell with concentrated cell sap is placed in pure water. Which change is most likely to occur?
options: Water enters the cell by osmosis and the cell becomes turgid.
There is no net movement of water because the concentrations are equal.
Water leaves the cell by osmosis and the cell becomes flaccid.
Water enters the cell by active transport and the cell bursts.
questions.explanation: Pure water has a higher water potential than the concentrated cell sap, so water moves into the cell by osmosis. The cell wall prevents the plant cell from bursting, and the cell becomes turgid.

questions.q: In a reflex arc, which neurone carries an electrical impulse from a receptor to the central nervous system?
options: Motor neurone
Sensory neurone
Relay neurone
Effector neurone
questions.explanation: Sensory neurones carry impulses from receptors to the central nervous system. Relay neurones pass impulses within the central nervous system, while motor neurones carry impulses from the central nervous system to effectors.

questions.q: Which change in the skin helps to reduce heat loss when the body is too cold?
options: Erector muscles contract, making hairs stand up and trap a layer of air.
Sweat glands release more sweat, which cools the skin as it evaporates.
Blood vessels in the skin widen, so more blood flows near the surface.
The body shivers, which increases heat loss by transferring heat to the air.
questions.explanation: Contracted erector muscles make hairs stand up and trap a layer of air, which reduces heat loss. Sweating and vasodilation increase heat loss, while shivering increases heat production rather than reducing heat loss.

questions.q: The kidneys help maintain a constant internal environment. Which waste product of protein breakdown do the kidneys remove from the blood?
options: Carbon dioxide
Glucose
Urea
Starch
questions.explanation: The liver breaks down excess amino acids to form urea, and the kidneys remove urea from the blood in urine. Glucose is useful and is reabsorbed, carbon dioxide is removed by the lungs, and starch is not normally present in the blood.
